1.q: בַּ⁠שָּׁנָה֙ הָ⁠עֲשִׂירִ֔ית בָּ⁠עֲשִׂרִ֕י בִּ⁠שְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר לַ⁠חֹ֑דֶשׁ
1.note: If your language would not represent numbers in forms such as **tenth** and **twelfth**, you could represent these numbers in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [In year ten, in month ten, on day twelve of the month]

The **tenth** month of the Hebrew calendar includes the last part of December and the first part of January on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.
See how you translated this expression in 20:2.

2.note: See how you translated **Son of man** in [2:1](ta:02). This also occurs in verse 18.
See how you translated the similar phrase in Ezekiel 4:3. Alternate translation: [make your face firm to Pharaoh]

3.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 2:4.

3.q: דַּבֵּ֨ר וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֜ כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֗ה הִנְ⁠נִ֤י עָלֶ֨י⁠ךָ֙
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Speak and say that the Lord Yahweh declares that he is against you]

Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Pay attention, I am against you, Pharaoh king of Egypt]

Yahweh is speaking as if Pharaoh were **the great sea monster lying in the midst of his rivers**. It means that Pharaoh was powerful and felt secure in Egypt, just as a large creature such as a crocodile lies safely in the channels of the Nile River. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the powerful ruler who feels secure in the midst of his rivers]

3.q: אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָמַ֛ר לִ֥⁠י יְאֹרִ֖⁠י וַ⁠אֲנִ֥י עֲשִׂיתִֽ⁠נִי
3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [who said that the Nile belonged to him and that he had made himself.]

This could mean: (1) Pharaoh was claiming that he had made the Nile for himself. Alternate translation: [; I made that river] or (2) Pharaoh was claiming that he had created himself, which would be a claim to be divine. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and I, I have created myself as a god]

4.note: Yahweh is speaking as if Pharaoh were a large river creature that Yahweh would catch by putting **hooks in your jaws**. It means that Yahweh will cause Pharaoh to be captured and take away his power. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will capture you and take away your power]

Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Egypt were **the fish of your rivers** that **cling to your scales**. It means that the Egyptian people, who depend on Pharaoh, will share in his defeat. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will make your people, who depend on you, share in your defeat]

5.note: Yahweh is using **the face of the field** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the surface of the open ground.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You will fall on the surface of the open countryside]

The expressions **you will not be gathered** and **nor will you be gathered together** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one will gather you, nor will anyone collect you together]

The terms **gathered** and **gathered together** mean similar things. Both refer to collecting a dead body in order to bury it. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [no one will ever collect your body for burial]

Yahweh is using the past tense **I have given** to refer to something that will happen in the future. He is doing this to show that the event will certainly happen. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the future tense here.

6.note: The implication is that when these things happen, the people will recognize that Yahweh is the true God, who has the power and authority to do what he has said he will do. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See the Introduction to Ezekiel for more information. Alternate translation: [I, Yahweh, am the true God who has the power to do what I said I would do]

6.q: יַ֧עַן הֱיוֹתָ֛⁠ם מִשְׁעֶ֥נֶת קָנֶ֖ה לְ⁠בֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
6.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the Egyptians were a **staff of reed** for the house of Israel. A reed is a weak plant that breaks easily, so a staff made from it would give way when someone leaned on it. It means that Egypt was unreliable and failed to support Israel when Israel depended on it. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because they were an unreliable source of help for the house of Israel]
See how you translated this phrase in [3:1](ta:03).

7.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the Israelites. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [When the Israelites grasped you by your palm]

The phrase **by your palm** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. There is, however, a correction in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended. You may want to follow this correction in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [by the palm]

The expressions **you were crushed** and **you were broken** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you splintered … you snapped]

The implication is that when the reed staff broke, its splintered pieces tore into the shoulder of the person who was holding it. This means that Egypt harmed the Israelites instead of helping them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and your splintered pieces tore into the shoulder of every one of them]

Here, **loins** represent “strength,” since the hips and lower back hold up a person’s body. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and you made all of them lose their strength]

8.q: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְ⁠נִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא עָלַ֖יִ⁠ךְ חָ֑רֶב
8.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [I, the Lord Yahweh, declare that I am surely bringing against you a sword]

Here, **a sword** represents “an army that will attack with swords.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [an army armed with swords]
See how you translated this expression in 25:13.

9.note: The terms **a desolation** and **a ruin** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [a complete wasteland]

9.q: וְ⁠יָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה יַ֧עַן אָמַ֛ר
9.note: The pronoun **they** refers to the people of Egypt, and the pronoun **he** refers to Pharaoh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the people of Egypt will know that I am Yahweh, because Pharaoh said]

9.q: יַ֧עַן אָמַ֛ר יְאֹ֥ר לִ֖⁠י וַ⁠אֲנִ֥י עָשִֽׂיתִי
9.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [because he said that the Nile was his and that he himself had made it]

10.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **ruins** that are characterized by **devastation**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [into completely devastated ruins, a desolation]

Yahweh is referring to all of the land of Egypt by naming its two extremes, **Migdol** in the north and **Syene** in the south, near **the border of Cush**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [throughout the whole country, from one end to the other]
The words **Migdol** and **Syene** are the names of towns. Migdol was in northern Egypt, and Syene was in southern Egypt.

11.q: לֹ֤א תַעֲבָר־בָּ⁠הּ֙ רֶ֣גֶל אָדָ֔ם וְ⁠רֶ֥גֶל בְּהֵמָ֖ה לֹ֣א תַעֲבָר־בָּ֑⁠הּ
11.note: Yahweh is using **The foot of man** and **the foot of beast** to represent whole people and animals. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [People will not pass through it, and animals will not pass through it]

The expression **it will not be inhabited** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people will not live in it for]

12.q: וְ⁠נָתַתִּ֣י אֶת אֶרֶץ֩ מִצְרַ֨יִם שְׁמָמָ֜ה בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ אֲרָצ֣וֹת נְשַׁמּ֗וֹת וְ⁠עָרֶ֨י⁠הָ֙ בְּ⁠ת֨וֹךְ עָרִ֤ים מָֽחֳרָבוֹת֙ תִּֽהְיֶ֣יןָ שְׁמָמָ֔ה
12.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will make the land of Egypt and her cities completely desolate, like the other ruined lands and cities around her]

12.q: בְּ⁠ת֣וֹךְ אֲרָצ֣וֹת נְשַׁמּ֗וֹת & בְּ⁠ת֨וֹךְ עָרִ֤ים מָֽחֳרָבוֹת֙
12.note: The expressions **desolated** and **laid waste** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [in the midst of lands that others have desolated … in the midst of cities that others have laid waste]

12.q: וַ⁠הֲפִצֹתִ֤י אֶת מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ בַּ⁠גּוֹיִ֔ם וְֽ⁠זֵרִיתִ֖י⁠ם בָּ⁠אֲרָצֽוֹת
12.note: The terms **scatter** and **disperse** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [And I will scatter Egypt far and wide among the nations]

In this verse, the word **Egypt** is singular in form, but it refers to all of the people of Egypt as a group. That is why Yahweh uses the plural pronoun **them**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a plural form such as “the Egyptians.” Alternate translation: [And I will scatter the Egyptians]

13.q: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֑ה מִ⁠קֵּ֞ץ אַרְבָּעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙
13.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [I, the Lord Yahweh, declare that from the end of 40 years]

The expression **they were scattered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it is clear from the previous verse that Yahweh did it. Alternate translation: [among whom I had scattered them]

14.note: Yahweh is using **restore the captivity** as a common expression of the culture to mean “cause to prosper again.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will make Egypt prosperous again]
The word **Pathros** is the name of a region in southern Egypt.

Yahweh is speaking as if Egypt would be a kingdom that was physically **lowly**, that is, low to the ground. It means that Egypt will be weak and unimportant. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And there they will be a kingdom with little power or importance]

15.note: Yahweh is speaking as if Egypt could physically **lift itself up** above other nations. It means that Egypt will never again make itself more powerful or important than other nations. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it will not make itself more powerful than the nations again]
Here, **so as** marks **not to rule over the nations** as the goal or purpose of **I will make them few**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

16.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **confidence**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [as something they trust in]

This could mean: (1) Egypt will no longer remind Yahweh of the sin that the Israelites committed when they **turned after them** for help instead of trusting him. Alternate translation: [reminding me of the sin that the Israelites committed] (2) Egypt will no longer remind the Israelites of the sin that they committed when they sought help from Egypt. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [reminding the Israelites of the sin that they committed]
If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **iniquity** and **remembrance**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [reminding me of how they sinned]

Yahweh is using **turned after them** as a common expression of the culture to mean “sought help from the Egyptians.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when they went to the Egyptians for help]

17.note: Ezekiel is using the phrase translated as **And it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

18.note: Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [made his army work very hard]

18.q: כָּל רֹ֣אשׁ מֻקְרָ֔ח וְ⁠כָל כָּתֵ֖ף מְרוּטָ֑ה
18.note: The expressions **Every head was made bald** and **every shoulder was made bare** are passive verbal forms. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state what did the action, it was the heavy loads that the soldiers carried. Alternate translation: [The heavy loads rubbed every head bald, and they rubbed every shoulder bare]

18.q: וְ֠⁠שָׂכָר לֹא הָ֨יָה ל֤⁠וֹ וּ⁠לְ⁠חֵיל⁠וֹ֙ מִ⁠צֹּ֔ר
18.note: If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **wages**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [But he and his army were not paid anything from Tyre]

18.q: וְ֠⁠שָׂכָר לֹא הָ֨יָה ל֤⁠וֹ וּ⁠לְ⁠חֵיל⁠וֹ֙ מִ⁠צֹּ֔ר
18.note: The implication is that by the time Nebuchadnezzar’s army captured Tyre, there was not enough wealth left in the city for the army to take as plunder to pay them for their long siege. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [But when Tyre fell, there was not enough wealth left in the city for him and for his army to take as wages]

19.q: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְ⁠נִ֥י נֹתֵ֛ן לִ⁠נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל אֶת אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם
19.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [I, the Lord Yahweh, declare that I am surely giving to Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon the land of Egypt]
See how you translated the similar expression in 25:4.

This could mean: (1) Nebuchadnezzar will carry away the wealth of Egypt, since the rest of the verse speaks of plunder and wages. Alternate translation: [And he will carry away her wealth] (2) Nebuchadnezzar will carry away the people of Egypt as captives. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And he will carry away her people]

Yahweh is using constructions in which each verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [and he will take everything valuable from her as plunder]

Yahweh is speaking as if the wealth of Egypt were **wages** that an employer pays to his workers. It means that Yahweh will allow Nebuchadnezzar’s army to take the wealth of Egypt as a reward for their work against Tyre. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And it will be a reward that his army receives for their work]

20.note: The implication is that Nebuchadnezzar and his army were acting as Yahweh’s agents when they attacked Tyre, because Yahweh was using them to punish that city. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [because they were acting for me when they punished Tyre]
The pronoun **they** refers to Nebuchadnezzar and his army. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Nebuchadnezzar and his army did it]
See how you translated **the declaration of the Lord Yahweh** in 5:11.

21.note: Yahweh is speaking as if the strength of the Israelites were **a horn** that he would make **sprout**. It means that Yahweh will make the Israelites strong again. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I will make the house of Israel strong again]

Here, **an opening of mouth** represents “the ability to speak freely.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and I will give you the ability to speak freely in their midst]
